newsitem.title: GERMANY: German police search but kidnap victim still missing.
newsitem.headline: German police search but kidnap victim still missing.

text.p: Police, who have arrested five suspected kidnappers and recovered a four million mark ($2.6 million) ranson, mounted a big search on Thursday but found no trace of abducted millionaire Jakub Fiszman.

They would not say whether the suspects were cooperating with their sweep through woods and fields east of Frankfurt but told reporters they hoped that Fiszman, who was kidnapped on October 1, was still alive.

"When we came here this morning we were optimistic we would find something, but it's such a big area to cover and we have to be careful that we are thorough," Ulrich Petri, a police spokesman at the scene, told journalists at midday.
He said the search would continue until nightfall. Asked whether police thought Fiszman was still alive, Petri said: "We are still hoping."
About 500 police with sniffer dogs combed the woods and fields in the Taunus area, 50 km (30 miles) from the German financial centre.

Police sealed off several hectares (acres) of land and barred journalists and television camera crews from entering the area in case they destroyed clues pointing to the whereabouts of the 40-year-old businessman.
Helicopters hovered overhead and police divers were brought in to search ponds in a huge operation which started at dawn.
At midday officers emerged from a densely-wooded hill empty-handed. "The first part of the search is over and has ended without success," Petri said.

Three German men and two women regarded by police as their main suspects were arrested on Wednesday and were due to appear before a Frankfurt court on Thursday where a judge would decide whether to detain them further.
The suspects are aged between 26 and 51 years. Police say more people may have been involved.
The only sign of life from Fiszman since he was abducted outside his Frankfurt office has been a telephone call the next day to a woman friend to say he was being held in a cellar.
Fiszman's brother Georg paid a ransom of four million marks ($2.6 million) on October 10, but his kidnappers reneged on an agreement and failed to free him the following day.
German police recovered the ransom money on Wednesday in the garden of a flat in Wiesbaden. Two 1,000 mark notes were ($650) missing.
